commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that the redrawn arrow is a different vector, because it starts somewhere new, for the arrow moving 2 right and 3 up.

fixIt.corrected: The redrawn arrow is the same vector: it still moves 2 right and 3 up, with magnitude sqrt(13) and the same direction. Free vectors slide: the same arrow drawn anywhere is the same vector.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state whether the arrow moving 2 right and 3 up is changed when it is redrawn at a new start point, and say what fixes a free vector.

commonErrors.misconception: Moving a vector to a new start point changes it.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks the statement that a redrawn free vector is a new vector, because its start point moved.

fixIt.corrected: It is the same vector: free vectors slide. Only position vectors are pinned to the origin, because a position vector is measured from the origin.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence why a free vector redrawn at a new point is still the same vector.

commonErrors.misconception: Moving a vector to a new start point changes it.

modelAnswers.question: Add a = (2, 3) and b = (1, -1), and state the column vector a + b.
Calculate the magnitude of the vector (6, 8).

nextSteps: Reteach the sliding point from the paired notes trap before any further vectors work: only a position vector is pinned to the origin.
Practise checking magnitude and direction first whenever an arrow is redrawn at a new start point.
strengths: Most of the class can add vectors component by component, such as a + b = (2 + 1, 3 + (-1)) = (3, 2) on the worksheet.
The class can find a magnitude by Pythagoras, such as |(6, 8)| = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 on the exit ticket.
